result.instructions:
KiCad MCP Server - A server for analyzing KiCad schematics and PCBs,
    and performing design rule checks.

    Available capabilities:
    - Schematic analysis (components, nets, symbols)
    - PCB analysis (footprints, tracks, statistics)
    - Design rule checking (ERC/DRC)
    - Schematic summarization
    - Hierarchical sheet and net tracing
    - Pin/power/bus extraction and device tree generation

tools.name: generate_device_tree
tools.description:
Generate device tree source (.dts) file from schematic.

This function analyzes a KiCad schematic and generates a device tree
source file compatible with the specified SOC family.

tools.name: extract_gpio_config
tools.description: Extract GPIO pin configurations from schematic.

tools.name: extract_i2c_devices
tools.description: Extract I2C bus and device configurations.

tools.name: extract_spi_devices
tools.description: Extract SPI bus and device configurations.

tools.name: extract_power_domains
tools.description: Extract power domain and regulator configurations.

tools.name: validate_pin_configuration
tools.description:
Validate pin configuration conflicts for device tree generation.

This function validates that the pin configuration is suitable for
device tree generation and reports any conflicts or issues.

tools.name: trace_hierarchical_connection
tools.description:
Trace component connections across hierarchical schematics.

This tool traces connections through the entire schematic hierarchy,
including sub-sheets, to show complete signal paths.

pin_number.description: Optional pin number to trace (if empty, trace all pins)

tools.name: analyze_hierarchical_nets
tools.description:
Analyze all nets in hierarchical schematic design.

This tool analyzes network connections across the entire hierarchy,
showing how signals flow between main schematic and sub-sheets.

filter_pattern.description: Optional regex pattern to filter net names

show_hierarchy.description: Whether to show hierarchical structure (default: True)

tools.name: generate_netlist
tools.description: Generate KiCad netlist from schematic file.

tools.name: trace_netlist_connection
tools.description: Trace component connections using netlist file (most accurate).

pin_number.description: Optional pin number (e.g., '1'). If empty, trace all pins.

tools.name: get_netlist_nets
tools.description: Get all nets from netlist file.

filter_pattern.description: Optional regex pattern to filter net names

tools.name: get_netlist_components
tools.description: Get all components from netlist with their network connections.

tools.name: search_parts_registry
tools.description:
Search an open registry of 21,000+ verified KiCad parts (no login).

Matches part id, name, family, category, manufacturer and keywords.
Example queries: "usb c connector", "0402 capacitor", "nrf9151".

query.description: Search terms (all terms must match; '*' wildcards allowed)

tools.name: get_registry_part
tools.description:
Get the full registry record for one part.

Includes download URLs (footprint/symbol/3D), datasheet link, dimension
provenance and field reports from real builds.

tools.name: download_registry_part
tools.description:
Download a registry part's files into a local directory.

Downloads are HTTPS-only, restricted to the registry's own hosts,
capped at 50 MB per file, and saved with extension-checked filenames.

save_dir.description: Existing local directory (e.g. the project library folder)

formats.description:
Which files — any of "footprint", "symbol", "step",
"preview" (default: footprint + symbol)

tools.name: list_pcb_footprints
tools.description: List all footprints in a KiCad PCB file.

tools.name: get_pcb_statistics
tools.description: Get statistics about a KiCad PCB design.

tools.name: analyze_pcb_nets
tools.description:
Analyze nets in a KiCad PCB file.

Provides track width distribution, via distribution, per-net track
length ranking, layer coverage, and design rule comparison.

tools.name: find_tracks_by_net
tools.description: Find track segments belonging to a specific net.

net_name.description: Name of the net to search for

tools.name: analyze_pcb_signal_integrity
tools.description:
Analyze signal integrity: diff pair matching, RF traces, critical nets.

Auto-detects differential pairs (e.g., USB_N/USB_P, DP/DN) and checks
length matching. Reports RF trace dimensions and longest signal nets.

net_name.description: Optional specific net to analyze in detail

tools.name: analyze_pcb_power_integrity
tools.description: Analyze power integrity: copper zones, power net routing, GND coverage.

tools.name: setup_pcb_layout
tools.description:
Initialize an empty PCB with the specified board outline dimensions.

Writes a .kicad_pcb next to the schematic containing only the board
outline (Edge.Cuts), a standard 2-layer stack and default design rules —
no footprints, tracks or nets. KiCad stores .kicad_pcb coordinates in
millimetres (plain decimals), so dimensions are emitted directly in mm.

schematic_path.description:
Path to the .kicad_sch the board is based on (used to
derive the .kicad_pcb path and board title).

width.description: Board width in the given unit.

height.description: Board height in the given unit.

tools.name: export_gerber
tools.description:
Export a PCB to Gerber + drill files for fabrication via kicad-cli.

Runs KiCad's command-line exporter against the .kicad_pcb and reports the
files actually produced. Requires KiCad 7+ installed with kicad-cli on PATH.

output_dir.description:
Directory for output (default: a "gerber" folder next to
the PCB).

tools.name: analyze_pin_functions
tools.description:
Analyze pin functions and detect conflicts.

This function analyzes schematic to determine pin functions by:
- Examining net names to infer functionality
- Identifying MCU components and their pin mappings
- Detecting potential pin conflicts

reference.description: Optional component reference (e.g., 'U1') to analyze specific component

tools.name: detect_pin_conflicts
tools.description:
Detect pins with conflicting electrical connections.

This function checks for:
- Multiple outputs on same net
- Power-to-power connections
- Unconnected input pins
- Pin type mismatches

tools.name: extract_pinmux_config
tools.description:
Extract pin multiplexing configuration for MCUs.

This function extracts pin multiplexing (pinmux) configuration
for MCU components, showing which peripherals are assigned to which pins.

tools.name: create_kicad_project
tools.description:
Create a new KiCad project.

By default the project is empty: a blank board, schematic and project
file written by the installed KiCad itself, so they are in its native
file format.

template.description:
"empty" (default) for a blank project, or a KiCad template
to start from, by name (e.g. "Arduino_Uno", "RaspberryPi-HAT") or
as a path to a template directory. Templates come with their own
board outline, footprints and schematic.

tools.name: list_schematic_components
tools.description: List all components in a KiCad schematic file.

filter_type.description: Optional filter by component type prefix (e.g., 'R', 'C', 'U', 'IC')

filter_value.description: Optional filter by component value (partial match)

filter_dnp.description: Optional filter by DNP flag (True=only DNP, False=only non-DNP)

tools.name: get_symbol_details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific symbol/component.

tools.name: search_symbols
tools.description: Search for symbols/components matching a pattern.

tools.name: list_schematic_nets
tools.description: List all nets in a KiCad schematic.

filter_power.description: If True, only show power nets (VCC, GND, etc.)

tools.name: get_schematic_info
tools.description: Get general information about a schematic file.

tools.name: add_hierarchical_label
tools.description:
Add a hierarchical label on a component pin (cross-sheet connection).

Hierarchical labels are how signals cross sheet boundaries in KiCad: a
label placed in a sub-sheet appears as a same-named pin on the parent
sheet's sheet symbol, connecting the two. Placing them by hand for
every cross-sheet signal is the classic tedium this automates.

The label anchors EXACTLY on the pin (computed from the embedded
symbol geometry incl. rotation and the library-vs-sheet Y flip), so
the connection is electrically valid — verify with generate_netlist.

file_path.description:
Path to the .kicad_sch file (the SUB-sheet for signals
going up to its parent).

label_name.description: Label text; defaults to the reference+pin when empty.

shape.description:
Electrical direction: input, output, bidirectional,
tri_state or passive (ERC uses this).

tools.name: add_global_label
tools.description:
Add a global label on a component pin (project-wide connection).

Global labels connect same-named signals anywhere in the whole
hierarchy regardless of sheets — useful for power-style rails and
cross-cutting signals where a hierarchical parent/child chain would
be awkward.

label_name.description: Global net name (required — globals are named nets).

shape.description:
Electrical direction: input, output, bidirectional,
tri_state or passive.

tools.name: add_component_from_library
tools.description: Add a component from KiCad's built-in library to the schematic.

tools.name: add_wire
tools.description: Add a wire (connection line) to the schematic.

tools.name: add_label
tools.description: Add a local label (text label) to the schematic.

tools.name: search_components_by_type
tools.description:
Search for components by type (OLED, sensor, display, etc.).

This tool intelligently searches for components by their type, value,
footprint, or network connections to identify specific component categories.

component_type.description: Type of component to search for (e.g., 'OLED', 'sensor', 'display', 'SPI', 'I2C')

search_in_subsheets.description: Whether to search in hierarchical subsheets (default: True)

tools.name: run_erc
tools.description:
Run Electrical Rules Check (ERC) on schematic.

Checks for:
- Unconnected pins
- Power conflicts
- Multiple outputs on same net
- Pin type mismatches

tools.name: run_drc
tools.description:
Run Design Rules Check (DRC) on PCB.

Checks for:
- Clearance violations
- Track spacing violations
- Missing connections
- Pad/footprint overlaps
- Board edge constraints

tools.name: get_erc_violations
tools.description: Get filtered ERC violations from schematic.

tools.name: get_drc_violations
tools.description: Get filtered DRC violations from PCB.

tools.name: export_erc_report
tools.description: Export ERC report to file.

tools.name: export_drc_report
tools.description: Export DRC report to file.

tools.name: render_pcb
tools.description:
Render a 3D view of the PCB to a PNG image.

Produces a photorealistic render of the assembled board via kicad-cli
(footprints must have 3D models assigned; otherwise plain board geometry
is rendered). Returns the image itself, so multimodal clients show it
directly — useful for AI-assisted layout review.

side.description: Camera side: top, bottom, left, right, front, back.

output_path.description:
Output PNG (default: <pcb>_render_<side>.png next to
the PCB).

quality.description: Render quality: basic (fast) or high (slower, raytraced).

rotate.description:
Optional board rotation 'X,Y,Z' in degrees for isometric
views, e.g. '-30,0,25'.

tools.name: export_pcb_3d
tools.description:
Export the PCB as a STEP 3D model for mechanical CAD handoff.

Includes board body, footprints and their assigned 3D models.

output_path.description: Output .step file (default: <pcb>.step next to the PCB).

board_only.description: Export only the board body, without component models.

tools.name: export_schematic_svg
tools.description:
Export schematic pages to SVG images.

Renders every page of the (hierarchical) schematic as an SVG file via
kicad-cli. SVGs are vector graphics — clients and humans can zoom into
any detail without quality loss.
